name: Qwen3.8-27B drafters: Tencent DSpine-b16 and NVIDIA Qwen3.5-4B draft

lineage.base_model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (target); DSpine is a new 5-layer draft, the NVIDIA draft is initialized from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B
lineage.family: Qwen3.8-27B speculative-decoding drafters (see qwen3.8-27b; the earlier official DFlash2 drafter z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 dates from 2026-08-15 and is not recorded separately)
lineage.how_derived: DSpine: parallel block drafter in which each layer passes predicted predecessor features to adjacent positions (carries causal dependencies through depth). NVIDIA: a complete small LM trained with NVIDIA Model Optimizer in external speculative decoding mode on 199,998 conversations whose target top-20 distributions were recorded

purpose: Lower decode latency of Qwen3.8-27B without changing its output distribution: both are draft models whose blocks the target verifies. Tencent's card positions DSpine against the official DFlash2 drafter; NVIDIA states the draft is intended for NVIDIA Groq 3 LPU deployments and loads in vLLM, SGLang and TRT-LLM.

license.name: Tencent DSpine: Apache-2.0; NVIDIA draft: NVIDIA Open Model Agreement
license.notes: The DSpine repo LICENSE is the standard Apache License 2.0 (head read, 2026-11-19). The NVIDIA repo has no LICENSE file and the Open Model Agreement text was not read; the card says it is ready for commercial or non-commercial use and the Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.8-27B parts are Apache-2.0. verified stays false because only one of the two texts was read.

architecture.kind: draft models for speculative decoding (DSpine 5-layer sliding-window block drafter; NVIDIA dense Qwen3.5-4B-based drafter)
architecture.attention: DSpine: 5 sliding-window layers (window 8192), hidden 5120, 32 Q / 8 KV heads, block size 16. NVIDIA draft: 32 layers (24 Gated DeltaNet + 8 full attention), hidden 2560, 4.21 B parameters, trained at sequence length 12,288
architecture.recurrent: NVIDIA draft: Gated DeltaNet; DSpine: none
architecture.drafter: this is the drafter; the Qwen3.8-27B target has its own MTP head
architecture.why_this_design: DSpine card: parallel drafting with dependencies carried through network depth gives longer accepted blocks than DFlash2 (acceptance 7.20 against 5.69 on GSM8K). NVIDIA card: a draft that is a complete LM with the target's tokenizer and a probabilistic drafting policy matched to the serving policy (temperature 1.0, top-k 20, top-p 0.95), trained on target distributions for rejection sampling.

variants.notes: official in the sense of Tencent (the Qwen team's own drafter is z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2, 3.85 GB)

pc-12gb.notes: the 27B target does not fit; an extra 4 to 8 GB of draft makes it worse

pc-16gb.notes: 27B Q4 (about 16 GB) already exceeds the 13.6 GB VRAM budget; a draft adds 4 GB (DSpine) at BF16, less quantized

pc-24gb.notes: 27B at Q4 plus DSpine 4 GB BF16 in 21.6 GB is tight; the NVIDIA 8.4 GB draft would need quantization

mac-32gb.notes: 27B Q4 about 16 GB plus 4 GB draft within 22 GB, little KV left

engine_support.notes: No GGUF. DSpine uses dynamic verification following DSpark (deepseek-ai/DeepSpec) and ReplaySSM for the recurrent layers of the target. Tona uses the target's MTP head; an external drafter would be new work.

benchmarks.name: Agent end-to-end throughput speed-up, SWE-bench Pro replay (xhigh)

strengths: Acceptance lengths well above the target's own MTP head (NVIDIA: 5.58 against 3.81 overall) and above DFlash2 (Tencent), both vendor numbers
Output distribution of the target is preserved by rejection sampling
weaknesses: Throughput numbers are batched server numbers (concurrency 8, B-class GPUs), not single-user consumer-GPU decode
Drafters cost 4 to 8 GB extra memory, which matters on 16 to 32 GB cards
soft.behavior: Block size 16 (DSpine) or 16 (NVIDIA acceptance table); DSpine needs dynamic verification and ReplaySSM, the NVIDIA draft samples probabilistically under the serving policy.
best_for: server or large-VRAM deployments of Qwen3.8-27B
avoid_for: 12 to 16 GB cards where VRAM is the limit
soft.maturity: DSpine 6.9k downloads, NVIDIA draft under 1k; both are about two weeks old.

tona_fit.reason: Prior art for our speculative decoding work on the Qwen3.8-27B target (acceptance 5.6 against 3.8 for the MTP head). The memory cost and recurrent-layer verification (ReplaySSM) make it a research input rather than an offer for 16 GB users.

sources.note: README, config.json and LICENSE head read
README and config.json read; no LICENSE file

open_questions: Single-user decode speed-up on a consumer GPU (all vendor numbers are server batches)
Whether either drafter can be quantized without losing acceptance
